items.prompt: The number of books read last month by $10$ students is $2, 1, 0, 2, 3, 1, 2, 0, 1, 2$. If you make a dot plot, how many dots sit above each value $0$, $1$, $2$, and $3$ on the number line?
items.answer: Above $0$: $2$ dots; above $1$: $3$ dots; above $2$: $4$ dots; above $3$: $1$ dot.

steps: A dot plot places one dot above a value on the number line for each time that value appears in the data.
Count how many times each value occurs.
Value $0$ appears at positions $3$ and $8$, so $2$ times: $2$ dots.
Value $1$ appears at positions $2$, $6$, and $9$, so $3$ times: $3$ dots.
Value $2$ appears at positions $1$, $4$, $7$, and $10$, so $4$ times: $4$ dots.
Value $3$ appears at position $5$, so $1$ time: $1$ dot.
Check: $2 + 3 + 4 + 1 = 10$ dots, matching the $10$ students.

items.prompt: A dot plot of the number of pets owned shows: $3$ dots above $0$, $4$ dots above $1$, $2$ dots above $2$, and $1$ dot above $4$. How many students are shown in the dot plot?

steps: Each dot represents one student, so add up all the dots, not the number of different values.
Total dots $= 3 + 4 + 2 + 1$.
The dot plot shows $10$ students.

items.prompt: A dot plot of daily absences shows: $5$ dots above $0$, $3$ dots above $1$, $2$ dots above $2$, and $1$ dot above $3$. On how many days were there at least $2$ absences?

steps: 'At least $2$' means $2$ or more, so include the dots above $2$ and above $3$.
Dots above $2$: $2$ days.
Dots above $3$: $1$ day.
Add them: $2 + 1 = 3$ days.
On $3$ days there were at least $2$ absences.

items.prompt: A histogram of quiz scores has these equal-width intervals and bar heights: $0\text{–}4$ (height $1$), $5\text{–}9$ (height $3$), $10\text{–}14$ (height $6$), $15\text{–}19$ (height $2$). How many quiz scores are shown in total?

steps: Each bar's height is the frequency: how many data values fall in that interval.
Add the heights of all the bars.
There are $12$ quiz scores in total.

items.prompt: A box plot of test scores shows $\min = 60$, $Q_1 = 70$, median $= 78$, $Q_3 = 85$, and $\max = 95$. Read off the median and the maximum score.

steps: On a box plot, the line inside the box marks the median, and the right whisker ends at the maximum.
The median is given directly as $78$.
The maximum is given directly as $95$.
So the median score is $78$ and the highest score is $95$.

items.prompt: Plant heights in centimeters are $3, 7, 8, 11, 13, 14, 16, 19, 22$. Using equal-width intervals of width $5$ starting at $0$ ($0\text{–}4$, $5\text{–}9$, $10\text{–}14$, $15\text{–}19$, $20\text{–}24$), give the bar height (frequency) for each interval.

steps: Sort each value into the interval that contains it, then count how many land in each.
$0\text{–}4$ contains $3$: $1$ value.
$5\text{–}9$ contains $7$ and $8$: $2$ values.
$10\text{–}14$ contains $11$, $13$, and $14$: $3$ values.
$15\text{–}19$ contains $16$ and $19$: $2$ values.
$20\text{–}24$ contains $22$: $1$ value.
Check: $1 + 2 + 3 + 2 + 1 = 9$, matching the $9$ heights.

items.prompt: A histogram of student heights (cm) has intervals $130\text{–}139$ (height $4$), $140\text{–}149$ (height $7$), $150\text{–}159$ (height $9$), $160\text{–}169$ (height $5$). How many students are at least $150$ cm tall? Can you tell exactly how many students are $152$ cm tall?
items.answer: $14$ students are at least $150$ cm tall. No, you cannot tell exactly how many are $152$ cm tall.

steps: 'At least $150$ cm' means the intervals $150\text{–}159$ and $160\text{–}169$.
Add their heights: $9 + 5 = 14$ students.
A histogram only shows how many values fall in each interval, not the individual values.
The interval $150\text{–}159$ has height $9$, but those $9$ students could be any heights from $150$ to $159$.
So we cannot determine exactly how many are $152$ cm tall.

items.prompt: Order the data $7, 3, 9, 5, 11, 8, 6, 10, 4$ from least to greatest and find the median.

steps: First sort the data from least to greatest: $3, 4, 5, 6, 7, 8, 9, 10, 11$.
There are $9$ values (an odd count), so the median is the single middle value.
The middle position is the $5$th value: $3, 4, 5, 6, \underline{7}, 8, 9, 10, 11$.
The median is $7$.

items.prompt: A box plot of quiz scores has $\min = 4$, $Q_1 = 7$, median $= 10$, $Q_3 = 13$, $\max = 18$. Compute the interquartile range (IQR).

steps: The interquartile range is $\text{IQR} = Q_3 - Q_1$, not $\max - \min$.
The IQR is $6$.

items.prompt: The data set $12, 15, 11, 18, 14, 20, 16, 13$ has $8$ values. Order it and find the median and the lower quartile $Q_1$.

steps: There are $8$ values (even), so the median is the average of the $4$th and $5$th values.
The lower half is the first four values: $11, 12, 13, 14$.
$Q_1$ is the median of the lower half: $\frac{12 + 13}{2} = \frac{25}{2} = 12.5$.
So the median is $14.5$ and $Q_1 = 12.5$.

items.prompt: Find the full five-number summary ($\min$, $Q_1$, median, $Q_3$, $\max$) and the IQR for the data set $5, 8, 2, 9, 6, 4, 7, 3, 10, 1$.

steps: $\min = 1$ and $\max = 10$.
There are $10$ values (even), so the median is the average of the $5$th and $6$th values: $\frac{5 + 6}{2} = 5.5$.
Lower half (first five values): $1, 2, 3, 4, 5$; its median is the middle value $3$, so $Q_1 = 3$.
Upper half (last five values): $6, 7, 8, 9, 10$; its median is the middle value $8$, so $Q_3 = 8$.
Five-number summary: $1, 3, 5.5, 8, 10$; IQR $= 5$.

items.prompt: Two classes take the same test. Class A's scores have a box plot with $Q_1 = 72$, $Q_3 = 88$. Class B's scores have a box plot with $Q_1 = 78$, $Q_3 = 84$. Compute each IQR and state which class has the more consistent (less spread out) scores.
items.answer: Class A IQR $= 16$; Class B IQR $= 6$. Class B is more consistent.

steps: The IQR measures the spread of the middle half of the data; a smaller IQR means more consistent scores.
Class A: $\text{IQR} = Q_3 - Q_1 = 88 - 72 = 16$.
Class B: $\text{IQR} = Q_3 - Q_1 = 84 - 78 = 6$.
Since $6 < 16$, Class B's middle half of scores is less spread out.
Class B has the more consistent scores.

items.prompt: A coach records the number of minutes each of $25$ players ran. She wants to show how the running times group into ranges (such as $0\text{–}9$, $10\text{–}19$, and so on) without listing every individual time. Which display, a dot plot, a histogram, or a box plot, is most appropriate, and why?
items.answer: A histogram, because it groups many values into equal-width intervals and shows the frequency in each range.

steps: A dot plot shows every individual value, which becomes cluttered and is not what is wanted here.
A box plot summarizes the data into five numbers but does not show how many players fall in each range.
A histogram groups data into equal-width intervals (bins) and uses bar heights to show the frequency in each range.
Since the coach wants to see how the $25$ times group into ranges, the histogram is the best choice.

items.prompt: You have the data set $14, 9, 22, 17, 5, 30, 11, 26, 19, 8, 24, 13$ (number of emails received per day). Choose a reasonable equal-width interval width starting at $0$, list your intervals, and give the bar height (frequency) for each. Explain why your number of bins is reasonable.
items.answer: Using width $10$ from $0$: $0\text{–}9$: $3$; $10\text{–}19$: $5$; $20\text{–}29$: $3$; $30\text{–}39$: $1$. Four bins is reasonable for $12$ values ranging $5$ to $30$.

steps: The data range from $5$ to $30$, so the full spread is about $25$.

A width of $10$ starting at $0$ gives intervals $0\text{–}9$, $10\text{–}19$, $20\text{–}29$, $30\text{–}39$: four bins, which is a manageable number for $12$ values (not so many that bars are empty, not so few that detail is lost).
$0\text{–}9$ contains $5$, $8$, $9$: height $3$.
$30\text{–}39$ contains $30$: height $1$.
Check: $3 + 5 + 3 + 1 = 12$, matching the $12$ data values.

items.prompt: Two soccer teams record goals scored per game over a season. Team X has five-number summary $2, 4, 5, 7, 9$ ($\min, Q_1, \text{median}, Q_3, \max$) and Team Y has $1, 3, 6, 8, 12$. Compare the two distributions: which team has the higher median, which has the greater IQR, and which has the greater overall range? State which team is more consistent.
items.answer: Team Y has the higher median ($6$ vs $5$), the greater IQR ($5$ vs $3$), and the greater range ($11$ vs $7$). Team X is more consistent.

steps: Compare medians: Team X median $= 5$, Team Y median $= 6$, so Team Y has the higher median.
Compute each IQR $= Q_3 - Q_1$. Team X: $7 - 4 = 3$. Team Y: $8 - 3 = 5$. Team Y has the greater IQR.
Compute each range $= \max - \min$. Team X: $9 - 2 = 7$. Team Y: $12 - 1 = 11$. Team Y has the greater range.
A smaller IQR (and smaller range) means less spread, so the data are more consistent.
Since Team X has the smaller IQR ($3 < 5$) and smaller range ($7 < 11$), Team X is more consistent.
